newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan backs Fujimori over Peru hostage crisis.
newsitem.headline: Japan backs Fujimori over Peru hostage crisis.

text.p: Japan's powerful Lower House of parliament on Wednesday unanimously adopted a resolution supporting Peruvian President Alberto Fujimori's handling of the Lima hostage crisis.

In what was a clear signal to leftist rebels holding the hostages, that Japan and Peru were united on how to handle the crisis, the resolution denounced the guerrillas for "conducting criminal acts against the international community".

Members of the Marxist Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) seized the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima on December 17, and over a month later were still holding 73 people, including the ambassador, hostage.

"We confirm the basic principle of not giving in to terrorism and urge the government to work toward a peaceful resolution of the crisis with the top priority on the lives of the hostages," the resolution adopted by the 500-seat Lower House said.
The mainly ceremonial Upper House is scheduled to pass a similar resolution on Thursday.
The resolution expressed "support for the Peruvian government's efforts to achieve a peaceful end to the crisis".
On Monday, in his opening speech to the 1997 session of parliament, Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto was equally unequivocal in his support for Fujimori's handling of the crisis.

"Japan will never give in to terrorism," Hashimoto declared. "Terrorist activity is a grave challenge to all states and societies and it is vital for the international community to tackle terrorism in unity."
Hashimoto also declared his "complete confidence" in Fujimori's hardline negotiating tactics in refusing to consider the rebels' main demand for the release of their comrades held in Peruvian jails.
